title: Credential brokering and secrets management
subtitle: No agent in my estate holds a credential it does not need, and most hold none.
lede: The usual way to give an agent access is a scoped token and hope. In Agent Swarm I wanted a plain property instead: an agent cannot call what it was not granted and never holds a credential it does not need. How sensitive an action is depends on which agent holds the credential for it, so I decide which agent may hold one, and every other agent asks that one for an outcome. Git is the domain with its own gatekeeper. A coding agent on a local open-source model edits, tests and pushes to its own branch in a throwaway container, then asks the gatekeeper persona to open a merge request.
evidence: Identity and least privilege for AI agents: a gatekeeper persona holds the git credential, and a coding agent on a local model opens merge requests without ever holding it.
Secrets management: operator tools that store, rotate, revoke, list and push secrets without ever returning a value, and no secret bytes in any log.
Credential isolation for managed AI seats: each seat's login held by reference in its own private state directory, never in an image or a log.
author: Corey James
